why: Adding the small binding to keep a preceding noun/verb head with an immediately following numeral/measurement made the model avoid cuts next to numeric tokens, which produced modest gains for short pieces (bins ≤3/5/7) but a slight decline on long spans (≤99); overall more (2019) pairs improved than worsened (1753) but the mean gain is small and not robust. The tail shows that the edit pulled cuts away from numeric/measurement attachments (e.g. keeping “5-3 win” or the “four times … and eleven times” grouping) and in some sentences forced cuts into nearby clause or enumeration boundaries, causing the worst drops.
lesson: A later revision should keep the immediate head+numeral/measurement binding only insofar as it benefits short segments, and avoid letting that binding shift cuts across clause boundaries or split enumerations in longer sentences.
